authoredPrompt: This figure contains six panels (a)–(f) illustrating the operation of insertion sort on an array of six integers. Each panel shows a horizontal array of six cells indexed 1 through 6 above the cells. Gray cells to the left of the current key represent the already-sorted subarray; the current key is shown in a black cell with white text; white cells to the right remain unsorted. Curved arrows below the array indicate element movements: a bold black arrow points to the slot where the key will be inserted, while lighter gray arrows indicate elements shifting one position to the right to make room. Panel (a) shows the initial array [5, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3] with key 2 at position 2 moving left past 5. Panel (b) shows key 4 at position 3 being inserted into sorted subarray [2, 5]. Panel (c) shows key 6 at position 4 requiring no movement as it is already the largest element in the sorted prefix. Panel (d) shows key 1 at position 5 shifting four elements rightward to reach position 1. Panel (e) shows key 3 at position 6 shifting three elements rightward to reach its correct position. Panel (f) shows the final sorted array [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] with no black cell and no arrows. This figure illustrates the insertion sort algorithm step by step, demonstrating how each key is extracted and inserted into its correct position within the growing sorted subarray to its left.

discrepancies: The default rendered figure is squeezed into the left side by a large workbench/code-editor UI, so the six panels are much smaller than in the source and the figure no longer reads like the standalone textbook image.
Panel (c) incorrectly shades cells 1 and 2 gray; in the source only the predecessor cell containing 5 is gray while the key 6 is black.
Panel (e) incorrectly shades cell 1 gray; in the source cell 1 remains white, while cells 2–5 are gray and cell 6 is black.
The generated figure adds a large insertion-sort programming workbench that is absent from the source and visually dominates the composition.
The curved arrows are simplified and thinner/smaller than the textbook arrows, especially the long black and gray arrows in panels (d) and (e).
evaluation.notes: The six-panel insertion-sort sequence is mostly recognizable and the interactive workbench is functional and meaningful, but the default view is far too small and some gray highlighting does not match the source.
action_items: Make the default static figure occupy the main canvas at textbook scale, ideally by docking or collapsing the workbench UI so the source-like figure is not reduced to a thumbnail.
Correct the gray highlighting in panel (c) so only cell 3 is gray, with cells 1 and 2 white.
Correct the gray highlighting in panel (e) so cell 1 remains white and only cells 2–5 are gray.
Increase figure label and index sizes relative to the rendered viewport so panel letters, indices, and cell values remain comfortably readable.
